conviction_note: Nothing sourced decides this print: consensus ($0.78-0.79 EPS, $82.8-82.9M revenue) sits on the Q2 adjusted run-rate and inside management's own Q3 frame (NIM flat, loans flat to slightly down, expense $41-43M, fee income $11.5-13M). A September Fed hike and an 87bp rise in the 10-year are a mild NIM and MSR tailwind that peers QCR and Old Second confirmed in primary documents. Softer acquired-loan accretion and central-Illinois ag credit stress pull the other way. Findings net to -0.15 and p_up is 51, so the scaled number is +0.06. The two measurements agree that this is close to a non-result. abs_move stays at about the name's median reaction (2.94%), nudged up because the hunters' sizes have run too small and the call may give the first Q4 NIM read after the rate hike.

positioning_check: No usable option chain (baseline options.status no_paired_strikes), so there is no skew. Short interest, from Equibles' FINRA series (https://equibles.com/stocks/hbt/shortinterest, read 2026-10-23): 1,159,079 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 8.0 days to cover, up from 243k on 2026-06-15 and 751k on 2026-07-31. That is about 3.2% of 36.37M shares outstanding. Benzinga's float basis put 243k at 1.39% of float, which implies a float near 17.5M and puts 1.16M near 6.6% of float. Much of the rise after 2026-08-10 fits merger-arbitrage shorting against the Tri-County deal (3.8M HBT shares to be issued). Arb shorts do not cover on an earnings print, so this is not a crowded directional short of the 18-23% kind. It is still enough to shrink negatives modestly. The 2026-10-15 settlement publishes 2026-10-26; Equibles' model estimate of 1.22M is a forecast. Tape: spot $36.19, 2.8% below the 52-week high, 20-day run-up -0.17%, 5-day +1.71%, 20-day realised vol 19.3%.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp in September 2026, and the 10-year rose about 87bp in Q3 to about 5.29%. Management guided flat NIM for Q3 on 2026-07-27, before both moves. Midwest peers that have reported show the tailwind in primary documents: QCR (Moline IL) NIM TEY +3bp to 3.58%, 'exceeded its guidance', and it called the September hike slightly accretive; Old Second (Aurora IL) NIM +4bp to 5.27% with deposit cost up only 2bp. HBT's Q2 NIM rose 12bp on fixed-rate loan and securities repricing, so the hike and higher reinvestment yields point to a Q3 NIM at or slightly above the flat guide and a constructive Q4 NIM comment on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-27): NIM +12bp and a $0.05 EPS beat, stock +3.91%. Q1 2026: NIM +8bp but GAAP EPS hit by $15.7M of merger costs, stock -1.31%. NIM upside has paid on this name when it shows in EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.78-0.79 equals the Q2 adjusted $0.78, so the street has modelled the flat-NIM guide and no rate tailwind. If the hike were priced, estimates would sit above the Q2 run-rate. The 20-day run-up of -0.17% shows no pre-print bid.
findings.independence: Old Second Q3 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000357173/000035717326000057/osbc-ex99d1.htm, 2026-10-21): NIM +4bp, deposit cost +2bp. Wintrust NIM 3.49%, in line with its guide (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Wintrust+Reports+Record+Q3+Net+Income+of+%24239.1+Million). Both are peer proxies, not HBT's own number. HBT's rate-sensitivity table could not be retrieved.

findings.finding: Acquired-loan discount accretion was $2.1M in Q2 against $1.0M in Q1, and management called it 'higher than expected'. That is about 13bp of Q2's 4.32% NIM by my arithmetic on $6.405B of average earning assets. With rates up sharply in Q3, prepayments on the CNB book should slow and accelerated accretion should fall back toward the Q1 pace. That would cost roughly $0.5-1.0M pretax, about $0.01-0.02 of EPS and 3-6bp of NIM, partly offsetting the rate tailwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history on accretion alone. Q2's higher-than-expected accretion was part of the beat that drew +3.91%.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus at the Q2 run-rate assumes Q2's accretion repeats. If the street expected it to fall back, Q3 EPS estimates would sit below $0.78.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000775215/000077521526000069/hbt-20260630.htm) shows $4.97M of net accretion for 1H26 and a $10.1M PCD non-credit discount at close. It is the same company and the same subject, so it is not independent of the release. The finding shares the rate premise with finding 1 but works through a different mechanism (prepayment speed, not repricing).

findings.finding: The revenue bar of $82.8-82.9M is about $2M (2.4%) above Q2's $80.9M. Management's own frame (NIM flat, loans flat to slightly down, fees $11.5-13M) gives roughly $81.5-82.5M including the extra day. Consensus therefore sits at or above the top of what the company guided, while EPS consensus of $0.78-0.79 sits inside it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue was $80.90M against an $80.36M estimate: a small beat alongside the EPS beat, stock +3.91%. Q4 2025 (2026-01-26): -2.94%. The baseline does not record that print's line.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and inside the guided frame. If the street had marked revenue to the guide, the revenue estimate would be near $81.5-82M, not $82.9M. The rate tailwind in finding 1, or a GAAP MSR gain counted as revenue, may close the gap.
findings.independence: Guide figures come from the Quartr Q2 call summary (https://quartr.com/events/hbt-financial-inc-hbt-q2-2026_Fepv6SgR). Benzinga's $82.8M agrees with MarketBeat. The finding partly offsets finding 1; both are sized net.

findings.finding: Higher Q3 rates mark HBT's $19.3M fair-value MSR asset up (Q2 was a -$0.75M mark). Old Second booked a +$0.62M MSR gain 'primarily the result of increased rates'. HBT's AFS book will also show a larger unrealised loss: Old Second's AOCI loss widened $11.5M, yet its TBV was flat at $14.75. Expect a GAAP fee-income gain of about $0.5-1.5M that management excludes from adjusted EPS, and roughly flat TBV against Q2's $17.60, because retained earnings offset AOCI.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MSR marks are adjusted out on this name. Q2 carried a -$0.8M mark and the stock still rose +3.91%. The market has looked through this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is small and below the adjusted line, so it is a fraction of operating value. A headline GAAP EPS above the adjusted figure could read as a beat in the first wire headline.
findings.independence: HBT's MSR balance and Q2 mark are in its Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000775215/000077521526000063/hbt-20260630ex991.htm). The rate premise is shared with finding 1.

findings.finding: Agricultural credit in HBT's footprint weakened through 2026. First Mid (Mattoon IL) reported Q2 agricultural downgrades from special mention to substandard on 'strained cash flows' while expecting no significant losses. The Chicago Fed's August 2026 AgLetter described weaker Q2 ag credit and the largest real fall in farmland values since 2016. After the CNB deal, HBT's agricultural and farmland loans are $594M, 12.5% of loans, double the $272M a year earlier. That raises the risk of criticized-loan migration or a qualitative reserve build in Q3, when HBT's Q2 provision was only $0.7M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HBT print in the baseline turned on credit. NPAs were 0.15% of assets at Q2 with net recoveries, so credit has not been a line this stock traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus assumes a provision near Q2's $0.7M. A $2-3M ag-driven reserve build would cost $0.04-0.06 of EPS and is not in a $0.78-0.79 estimate. It is a proxy, though, and the rest of HBT's book is very clean (NPAs 0.15%), so it is sized small net of that.
findings.independence: Chicago Fed AgLetter, August 2026 (https://www.chicagofed.org/publications/agletter/2025-2029/august-2026). This is a proxy for HBT, not its own number. HBT's Q2 release reports a $3.9M increase in qualitative reserves, consistent with caution but not tied to ag.

findings.finding: HBT signed the Tri-County Financial merger agreement on 2026-08-10 and filed an S-4, an S-4/A and a 424B3 in Q3. Legal, advisory and filing costs will land in Q3 GAAP expense, with management likely to exclude them from adjusted EPS. That is a small GAAP-versus-adjusted gap on top of Q2's $0.3M of residual CNB costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 2026, $15.7M of CNB merger costs crushed GAAP EPS to $0.34 against $0.68 adjusted; the stock fell only -1.31%. The market looks through merger costs here.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is unquantified and adjusted out, worth almost nothing to the reaction. It is filed for completeness.
findings.independence: The Tri-County 8-K of 2026-08-10 is listed in EDGAR (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000775215&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). It is the same deal.

findings.finding: Short interest rose almost fivefold from 243k shares (2026-06-15) to 1.16M (2026-09-30, 8.0 days to cover, about 6.6% of float on Benzinga's float basis). The rise has run steadily since the July print and the August deal announcement. Part of it is likely merger-arb shorting that will not cover on a print, but 8 days of cover on a thin name (127k shares a day) adds a small squeeze mechanism to any beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior HBT print with comparable short interest. Short interest was 0.4-0.5% of shares in early 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: FINRA data is public, but the arb composition is unknown. If the short were directional and seen as crowded, the stock would not sit 2.8% below its 52-week high on flat momentum. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Benzinga gives 243,367 shares, 1.39% of float, at 2026-06-15 (https://it.benzinga.com/quote/HBT/short-interest). Same FINRA origin.

findings.finding: Capital return: the dividend was raised $0.02 to $0.25 in Q2. Only 15,466 shares were repurchased in Q2, and $14.0M remains under a $30M authorization that expires 2027-01-01. With a stock-for-stock deal pending (Tri-County vote 2026-10-29), buybacks are likely constrained, so no capital-return surprise is expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 dividend raise came with the +3.91% print, mixed with a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. No change is expected. Filed so the panel sees the capital line was checked.

outside_window.finding: The Tri-County Financial shareholder vote is 2026-10-29, and close is expected in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027. Vote approval removes deal-completion risk but falls after the exit window. About 28% of shares are already locked up to vote in favour.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The stock sits 2.8% below its 52-week high with a flat 20-day run-up, and my evidence is roughly balanced (rate tailwind against accretion fade and ag credit), so nothing here cuts strongly against the tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): finding 1 (rates) cut from +0.6 to +0.5, kept because QCR and Old Second confirm it in primary documents; lands_on set to guidance.
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): finding 3 (revenue bar against the company's frame) moved toward 0, from -0.3 to -0.2.

Rules 7 and 9 (short interest checked before negatives; size a segment net of the rest): finding 5 (ag credit) cut from -0.4 to -0.3, because the rest of the book is clean (NPAs 0.15%) and short interest of 8 days to cover argues for smaller negatives.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): Benzinga and MarketBeat agree, so the bar counts as sourced and no cap applies. The AAII $0.73 row was rejected as mislabelled.
The other findings, abs_move_pct 3.2 and p_up 51 were left unchanged. Sum moved from -0.25 to -0.15; the scaled number stayed at +0.06.
